answer: To register a worker, an operator must route a 3,500-unit bond through a public settlement inlet that only releases after three established accounts, each at least 200 days old, also lock 700 units for 45 days. If later clustering shows the new key shares a controller with an older one, all four locks are slashed. One honest seat therefore risks 5,600 units; standing up 400 aliases would freeze 2.24 million units and require 1,200 independent backers, far more than a week of fees can repay. A dry shale ledge and a carved jade token left in a mailbox do not open that settlement path.
